PullRequest.Title: sessions: focus the main window and moved chat after Move to Main Window
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347102

After **Move to Main Window**, the moved chat was not focused. Two things were wrong:

1. The main Agents window was never raised, and the active pane's focus was deferred while another window held focus. `SessionsChatWindowProvider.moveToMainWindow` now, after opening the moved chats and editors, focuses the main window and then the active session. With several chats moved together, the first moved chat is re-opened (without focus) so it is the active one, matching `openMovedChats` order. Only user-initiated move paths reach this method; close, quit and restore paths are guarded and unchanged.
2. Root cause of the remaining failure on real focus: the `setContext` autorun in `ChatGroupView` swaps the content view when the pane's kind changes (for example new session to chat). That detached the focused input, so focus fell to `BODY`. `ChatGroupView` now remembers whether focus was inside the old view and, once the new view is installed, focuses it. This only happens when the old view's own document is the one that has window focus (an injectable `_hasWindowFocus` predicate, the same pattern `ChatGroupsView` already uses), so a background or other-window chat never claims focus. Focus elsewhere in the same window, such as another group, the sidebar or the editor, is left untouched.

How to test: open a chat in a new window, use **Move to Main Window** in the chat window header; the main window comes to front with the moved chat shown and its input focused. Also move two chats of the same session together; the first should be focused.

Tests:
- Provider tests for the focus calls, with the skip logic unchanged.
- `ChatGroupView` tests with a real DOM: focus inside the old view is restored in the new view after a swap; focus elsewhere in the same document is left alone; a stale `activeElement` in a document that does not have window focus is not restored.
- `sessionsManagementService.test.ts` "detaching a chat without dragging creates a pane that survives closing its parent": its `retained` check used `getFocusedSessionView()`, which follows DOM focus and only passed by accident (nothing was focused). It now captures the two pane elements before the parent closes and asserts exactly one stays connected and is the sole remaining pane. It no longer depends on focus or on which pane is active, which differs between the Electron and browser runners.

Validation:
- Electron runner, `sessionsManagementService.test.ts`: 445 passing
- Browser runner, `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --browser chromium`: 444 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on `sessionsChatWindowProvider.test.ts`, `chatGroupsView.test.ts`: 203 passing (on the fix commits, before the test-only follow-ups)
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: exit 0
- Live check on a full build in a throwaway profile with real OS focus: PASS for a single chat move (main frontmost, `document.hasFocus()` true, `activeElement` in the moved chat's input, stable when sampled every 300 ms for 3 s) and for a normal session switch while typing in main (no unexpected focus jump; weak check). Before the fix `activeElement` was `BODY`.
- NOT RUN live: same-session multi-chat move (two chats of one session could not be created through the UI; covered by the provider and `ChatGroupView` tests and a reviewer trace), and the drag-out path.

Scenarios.Scenario: User moves one or more chats, and any companion editors, from a chat window into the main Agents window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command closes the source window, resolves moved chats, opens the first chat and remaining chat groups/sessions, restores companion editors, optionally reselects the first chat, then awaits main-window focus before focusing the active session. All newly added work is on this interaction's critical path; the host focus must complete before DOM focus is assigned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus the native main window through IHostService/nativeHostService.focusWindow; browser builds call Window.focus directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call per successful user-initiated move, independent of the number of chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No host-focus boundary was invoked by SessionsChatWindowProvider after moving chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly awaited immediately before focusing the active session, so its single round trip contributes to move completion latency but is required to raise the destination window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the first session through registered providers and re-open/reselect its first chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional provider-resolution chain only when at least two chats move; it does not grow with chat count. The normal moved-chat scenario is warm because the session was already displayed in the source chat window, and transcript reopening is a no-op unless an existing load failure has an explicit retry action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: openMovedChats performed the first resolution/open once; there was no final reselection call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequentially awaited before host focus. Existing openMovedChats already resolves and opens the first chat; the added call repeats selection so the original first chat is active after opening the rest.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open serialized companion editor inputs in the main editor group, which can load their backing resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched openEditors request containing the editors captured from the moved window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editors were opened after moved chats with the same restore-state wait and batched openEditors call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before destination-window focus. The diff extracts the unchanged editor restoration into a helper and preserves its prior placement after openMovedChats.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of chats and companion editors in the one window being moved. Existing chat placement/editor restoration scales with those collections; the diff adds only one extra chat reselection for N>1 and one host-focus call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The move path is serialized with await. Same-session side chats are already opened sequentially; distinct sessions are grouped before placement. The diff adds no parallel burst or unbounded queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chats and sessions are normally warm because they were visible in the source window. Session-resource providers use already surfaced/session-cache state on this path; the second open does not reload an already displayed transcript, and there is no new cache or retained key. Cold legacy migration can cross an agent-host boundary, but a chat already hosted in the window has normally completed that resolution, so the added call uses surfaced state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the exact constant call counts and sequential critical path from the changed method and service implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native focus latency varies by platform and provider-resolution cost varies by provider, but both added operations have fixed cardinality per explicit move and no realistic scaling or burst mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added constant work is necessary to raise and focus the destination and preserve the intended active-chat order; it does not fan out with moved-chat cardinality or cause repeated transcript loading.

Scenarios.Scenario: A visible chat group changes presentation kind, such as a new-session composer becoming a chat after a request starts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The group's reactive autorun computes the desired kind, creates and installs the replacement view, lays it out, binds the chat, and now restores focus only if the detached old view contained focus and that document still owns window focus.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One affected ChatGroupView per presentation-kind transition. The added ancestry check walks only the focused element's DOM ancestors within that group, and focus is invoked once per actual replacement rather than on every autorun update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work in the autorun; no async fan-out, queue, IPC, filesystem, database, subprocess, or network boundary is reached by the added focus predicate/action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or introduced. Existing view construction and transcript binding behavior is unchanged; the added state is a transient boolean.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the replacingView guard, DOM ancestry/window-focus predicates, and direct ChatView/NewChatView focus implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser focus can trigger style/focus-event work dependent on listeners, but this occurs once at a user-visible view replacement and only when focus was already inside the replaced subtree.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous DOM work is bounded to actual view replacement and restores focus rather than adding per-render, per-frame, or collection-scaling work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Updated browser tests capture retained pane DOM elements and exercise focus restoration/provider focus ordering.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test-only setup and assertions; no production workflow reaches these changed test expressions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed-size test fixtures with two pane elements or a few synthetic chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Test awaits remain serialized; no production concurrency changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No production cache behavior is affected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from file locations and test-suite declarations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to shipped performance because these files execute only in tests.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced the two production paths. The PR adds bounded, user-triggered focus/reselection work with fixed cardinality and no unbounded retention, fan-out, concurrency burst, or hot-loop UI regression. It does not fix a performance regression, so no regression-fix record or finding was submitted.
